title: Tracking historical changes in trustworthiness using machine learning analyses of facial cues in paintings
summary: Random-forest models estimated perceived trustworthiness from facial cues in historical paintings and found a small upward trend over time and an association with GDP per capita. A correction narrows the claim to perceived ratings, not actual sitter trustworthiness or social trust; the portrait samples and rater agreement limit interpretation.
ai_technology: Random-forest models estimate perceived trustworthiness ratings from facial cues in historical portraits.
organization: Laboratoire de Neurosciences Cognitives, Département d'études cognitives, ENS, PSL, Research University, INSERM, Paris, France. .

evidence.tested: The corrected study analyzed facial cues and human ratings across two portrait collections, reporting a small temporal trend in perceived trustworthiness and an association with GDP per capita.
evidence.unknown: The correction narrows interpretation to perceived facial ratings. Elite portrait samples and limited human-rater agreement constrain generalization; actual sitter trustworthiness and social trust were not measured.
evidence.ai_role: Random-forest models estimate perceived trustworthiness ratings from facial cues in historical portraits.
